acceptance.sentence: The stretch was one-sided: only the lower side was stretched. On the scored past dates it held 88.9% of actuals against a target of 80%. The six-month factors rest on 11 past six-month forecasts, of which 1 could be scored. The lower edge was floored at zero for: Q4FY26.

ranges.method: Each side's factor is the ceil(90% of n)-th smallest of the factors the n eligible past forecasts would have needed: the plain empirical rule, not a finite-sample guarantee. Six-month factors come from overlapping forecasts (each shares five of its six months with its neighbors) and are noisier: 11 past six-month forecasts to learn from, 1 scored.
ranges.reason: pooled over 1 and 3 months, 18 scored folds: simulated 7 held (39%), stretched 16 held (89%); the stretched coverage is closer to 80% and no horizon is more than 10 points further
ranges.rule: adopted if there are at least 6 scored folds at 1 and at 3 months, pooled 80% coverage over 1 and 3 months is closer to 80% than the simulated range's on the same folds, and no horizon (1, 3 or 6 months) moves more than 10 points further from 80%; each side's factor is the smallest, never below 1, that would have put at least 90% of the eligible past folds inside on that side (a fold is eligible once its whole horizon has ended; at least 5 are needed)

recency.reason: lower mean absolute error at 1 and 3 months (1m: 3,234,094 vs 4,398,197; 3m: 11,625,581 vs 12,417,199)
recency.rule: adopted only if the fitted model's mean absolute error is lower than the Goal 1 fit's at both 1 and 3 months, on the same folds (at least 6 at each)

backtest.reason: the model's mean absolute error is not lower than every baseline: 3m: model 11,625,581 vs trailing run-rate 8,100,541
backtest.scoring: per horizon, mean absolute dollar error over all folds; 'yes' only if the fitted model's error is lower than both baselines at 1 and 3 months; under 6 folds is 'not enough history to say'

fiscal_year.why_they_differ: Meeting every quarter's own target is stricter than meeting the year's total: a quarter that is ahead cannot lend its surplus to one that is behind, and pipeline created in a quarter mostly books after it.

lead_time.basis: the production forward function's own timing, on a probe dollar-amount created evenly through the month; independent of the capacity decision. These are dollar yields, not probabilities: amounts change between creation and win, so they can exceed or fall short of what the deal counts imply and are not forced to sum to one

count_outcome.meaning: of the deals created, from the fit in use; counts, so these sum to one

lead_time.question: of a dollar of pipeline created next month (at its first recorded amount), the cents booked by the end of each of the next four quarters

required_pipeline.meaning: 'required' means achievable inside the model's bounds (fitted conversion and timing, the cap above), not operationally achievable
required_pipeline.method: one deterministic solve in quarter order; each quarter's pipeline is created evenly on every day from the day after the as-of date to its end (creation starts now), and meets that quarter's target given its actual bookings, the pipeline already open and what earlier quarters were assigned; an unreachable quarter is assigned nothing. Pipeline assigned to a later quarter is also created in the earlier quarters' months, so it can only add to them

per_rep_rule.why: capacity was not shown to explain pipeline in this history, so the per-ramped-AE-month comparison is a diagnostic only and does not decide; the cap and the total rate do

required_pipeline.too_late_rule: a quarter is too late to fund with new pipeline when its requirement is over the cap (or the cap is used up, or no pipeline created in time can book inside it), or when everything created in its span (expected, earlier quarters' assignments and its own requirement) per day is above the team's best four-quarter average of total created pipeline per day, or, only where capacity is the forecast's basis, when that total per ramped AE-month is above the team's best; the reason names exactly the legs that fired

worksheet.definition: What moves the outcome: four operating drivers, each changed alone for deals created after the as-of date, measured around the plan in force.

drivers.applies_to: The share of deals created after the as-of date that are won, for organic, hire-generated and program pipeline alike. Open deals and actuals are untouched.

evidence.gate: A quarter counts when its deals have had the full horizon to win and at least twenty deals were created in it.

historical.rule: The low and high settings are the means of the lower and the upper half of the observed quarters; with an odd number of quarters the middle one is in neither half.

drivers.label: Win rate of new pipeline
drivers.limitation: The fit in use learns from every deal created in its recent window, young deals included, while these quarters are complete and matured, so they are older than that fit and may not describe it.

needed_alone.history_label: Beyond any observed quarter: the value lies outside the lowest and the highest quarter observed, so reaching it is an extrapolation that the history does not show.
needed_alone.outcome_label: Solves mathematically: this value, alone, takes fiscal-year bookings to target.

drivers.unit_label: dollars of ARR per won deal

drivers.applies_to: Organic deals created per day after the as-of date. The capacity term is not in use for this company, so headcount is not tied to creation here. Open deals and actuals are untouched.

evidence.gate: A quarter counts when at least twenty deals were created in it and there was capacity to divide by. Creation is final the day a quarter ends, so there is no waiting.

historical.rule: The low and high settings are the means of the lower and the upper half of the observed quarters; with an odd number of quarters the middle one is in neither half.

drivers.limitation: Each quarter is organic deals created per day of the quarter; the capacity term is not in use, so headcount plays no part.

needed_alone.outcome_label: Solves mathematically: this value, alone, takes fiscal-year bookings to target.

evidence.gate: A quarter counts when its deals have had the full horizon to win and at least five of them were won.

drivers.label: Cycle length of new pipeline
drivers.limitation: The fit in use learns from every deal created in its recent window, young deals included, while these quarters are complete and matured, so they are older than that fit and may not describe it. A quarter's cycle is the plain mean days of its wins, while the fit in use weights each day, so the two are close in kind but not the same measure.

needed_alone.history_label: Beyond any observed quarter: the value lies outside the lowest and the highest quarter observed, so reaching it is an extrapolation that the history does not show.
needed_alone.outcome_label: Solves mathematically, stepped: win times are whole days, so there is no exact root. This is the largest setting that reaches the target, and it overshoots by the amount shown.

worksheet.expectation_note: Every figure here is an expected value from the forward function. No simulation is run, so no range is attached to any sensitivity.
worksheet.history_note: Historical settings describe what the company has done. They are not forecasts, they are not called achievable, and nothing here says they will happen again.
worksheet.measured_around: the plan in force: its hires and program pipeline, as applied
worksheet.sensitivity_note: Each change is a conditional change in expected bookings, measured one driver at a time around the plan in force. It is not a forecast and not a cause, and the bars are never summed: drivers act together, not alone.
